thread:
alex: heads up — we've been seeing a bunch of failing deployments in the GPU clusters since the 04:00 deploy window. app pods CrashLoop because several expected env vars are missing (:frowning:)
samir: seeing the same in eu-west-1-gpu. node autoscaler reports low utilization but pods stay pending -> then start with missing LICENSE_KEY env and exit.
jenna: do we know which secret/provider those envs come from? sealed-secrets or sops? last change to pipeline was the Vault token rotation last night.
alex: values.yaml is sops-encrypted in the repo, decrypted by CI before we push to the GitOps repo. But the runtime config (runtime-license secret) is created via a sealed-secret workflow that relies on the sealed-secrets controller to unseal at apply time.
kevin: i pulled the ArgoCD logs — decryption step is failing intermittently:  
```
argocd-repo-server: failed to render manifests: sops failed: error unlocking with age: unable to fetch key from vault: 429 rate limit
```
samir: 429 from Vault? that would explain intermittent missing values. how many requests are we making during reconcile?
alex: looks like when a big rollout happens (we had 40 model servers spin up) ArgoCD/flux concurrently hits Vault to decrypt many files. Vault client got throttled; some decrypts fail and ArgoCD still applies the partial manifest set so the sealed-secret that contains LICENSE_KEY never makes it through.
jenna: and because the app fails fast, autoscaler thinks capacity isn't used properly and scales wrong -> GPU shortage events cascade. rough chain: decrypt race -> missing secret -> pod crash -> autoscaler misreads -> capacity shortages.
ops-bot: incident note: #GPU-capacity spike correlated at 2026-02-27T04:01:00Z with multiple failed decrypts (vault 429).
kevin: quick reproduction: run 30 parallel `sops -d` calls against repo via the same Vault token, you can hit the rate limit in <60s.
alex: proposed short-term mitigations: 1) add retry+backoff to the gitops decryption step, 2) gate apply until all templates render (fail-fast better than partial apply), 3) throttle concurrency of reconciles for large deployments.
samir: medium-term: introduce a local cache agent (vault-agent or sops-wrapper) on repo-server pods to multiplex a single token and avoid hitting Vault for every file. also raise token quota with security (we rotated tokens so need to coordinate).
jenna: ops ask: can we add a pre-sync hook in ArgoCD to check for presence of required sealed-secrets before applying model servers? e.g., `argocd app wait-for-condition` or a `preSync` job that validates rendered manifests.
alex: yeah I sketched a preSync hook that runs `sops -d` and verifies `kind: Secret` with `metadata.name: runtime-license` exists. If not, fail the sync. snippet:  
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: validate-secrets
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: check
        image: alpine/sops
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","sops -d /manifests/values.yaml | yq e '.data.LICENSE_KEY' - || exit 1"]
```
kevin: also add more granular observability: count vault 429s per repo-server, and alert if >5 in 1m.
samir: i've opened a PR to add exponential backoff + 429 handling to our `gitops-decryptor` library and to change the ArgoCD app to fail the sync on render errors: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gitops/pull/482
alex: can someone coordinate with security on raising the Vault request ceiling or add a client-side token cache? pinging @jenna too.
jenna: I'll take the security coord. I'll also add the preSync hook to the argocd app manifest and schedule a warm-up job for the sealed-secrets controller so keys are hot before big rollouts.
ops-bot: action created: INFRA-2143 "Add sops decrypt retry + argocd preSync validation for runtime secrets" assigned to samir, due 2026-03-05.
samir: i'll deploy the patched decryptor to staging and run a 100-parallel-decrypt loadtest.
alex: thanks all — if anyone sees more failing deploys, drop logs here (argocd-repo-server, vault-agent, sealed-secrets-controller). tagging oncall if it spikes again.
kevin: quick note for postmortem: link to logs + capacity graph: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/cluster/gpu?from=now-6h
alex: adding to postmortem checklist: avoid wide parallel reconciles during peak traffic and ensure decrypt-backoff + preSync validation in prod.
